1  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal challenging the quantum of compensation determined by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Chincholi, in MVC No.701/2018 vide judgment and award dated 28.04.2022.
2.
When the claimant and others were traveling in a Tempo Trax bearing registration No.KA-34/A-2042, the driver of the vehicle dashed against concrete barricade on a bridge.
As a result, the claimant suffered injuries and was shifted to Dr.Kamareddy Hospital, Kalaburagi, where she was treated as in-patient from 20.09.2017 to 24.12.2017.

It was claimed that the claimant had suffered fracture of mid shaft radius, ulna of left side, fracture of lower end of tibia and fibula of left side, fracture of wrist of left side and other injuries.
The claimant underwent surgery.
She was thereafter treated as an outpatient.

She alleged that the injuries were caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the aforesaid vehicle and therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation of Rs.21,50,000/- with interest at 12% p.a.

She claimed that she was an agricultural coolie and she was earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to the accidental injuries, she was permanently disabled and was not able to involve in any other work.
3. The claim petition was opposed by the insurer who denied the accident, injuries, age, income and occupation of the claimant.
It alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle had violated the terms of the policy and that he did not possess valid and effective driving licence.
It also alleged that compensation claimed by the claimant was excessive.
4. The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P13.
She examined the doctor who treated her as PW.2.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
It held that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident.

Consequently, it considered her notional income at Rs.10,250/- per month and assessed the disability suffered by her at 15% to the whole body and awarded the following compensation:

4. Towards medical expenses 3,00,200/-
and future medical expenses 5.

Towards loss of income 30,750/-
during treatment 6. Deprivation of future 60,000/-
amenities Total 8,28,290/-
6.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimant contends that the tribunal has committed an error in determining the disability at 15%, though PW.2 deposed that the claimant had suffered permanent injury and that the disability was to the extent of 70% to the whole body.
He submits that the tribunal committed an error in awarding meager compensation towards attendant, food and conveyance charges.
He also submits that the claimant was to undergo future medical treatment and the tribunal committed an error in awarding compensation towards that.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer submits that though the claimant had suffered injury,
the evidence of PW.2 disclosed that there was union of the fracture and having regard to the age of the claimant, it is impossible to accept her contention that she cannot engage in any agricultural activity.
He submits that the tribunal determined the compensation by considering the notional income of the claimant @ Rs.10,250/- per month and the disability at 15% to the whole body.
He submits that there is no reason to enhance the compensation.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. The fact that the accident occurred on 20.09.2017 is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered extensive injuries.
These injuries probabalize the claim that she could not engage herself in any activity.
It is found from the records that the claimant was an inpatient between 20.09.2017 to 24.12.2017.
It is therefore evident that the claimant was deprived of income for a period of 112 days but the tribunal had awarded loss of income during treatment only for a period of three months.
The compensation awarded under the conventional heads is just and reasonable.

Insofar as claim the disability suffered by the claimant, though PW.2 deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 70% to the whole body, having regard to the fact that the claimant did not undergo any amputation but only suffered fracture which did not render her completely unfit to carry on activity, the disability assessed by the tribunal is just and proper.
In that view of the matter, compensation of Rs.8,28,290/- determined by the deserves to be globally enhanced to a sum of Rs.8,50,000/-.
Eramma W/O Nagendrappa vs Khaja Moinoddin S/O Shaik Hussain And ... on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73133389/

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.8,28,290/-
awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by a sum of Rs.21,710/-, which is payable by respondent No.2 - Insurance Company along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation along with interest before the tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, it shall be released to the claimant.
